ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-CP-01: Operator precedence bug in FixedHelper.withdrawLiquidity:69 (redeposited0 | redeposited1 == 0)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Solidity 0.8.24 parses `a | b == 0` as `(a | b) == 0` in if-context because `uint256 | bool` is a type error — the compiler resolves the only valid grouping. Fuzz test over all uint256 confirms equivalence.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-CP-02: snapPrice initialized tick boundary check at exact target tick
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: The `>` check (line 264) for lte direction is correct by Uniswap V3 tick semantics. Landing AT a tick means you haven't crossed it — the tick's liquidityNet is applied on crossing, not on landing. The asymmetry between lte (>) and !lte (<=) is intentional.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-CP-04: Fee skew from dust in _splitAmountsAndFeesByHeight denominator
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: When totalAmountOutFilled > amountOut, the dust (bounded by 1 input unit's output) inflates the denominator in the fee split by a few wei. This shifts ~1-3 wei of fee from output-height LPs to input-height LPs per dust-producing swap. Bounded by dust amount, not compounding, informational only.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-CP-06: Last height gets accumulated rounding remainder in fee distribution loop
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Sequential mulDiv floor rounding in _increaseHeight/_decreaseHeight means the last height receives the accumulated truncation remainder. The difference per call is bounded by (K-1) wei where K = heights crossed. At high fee/amount ratios the absolute diff can be larger but remains proportional to feeAmount/numHeights. Not exploitable — dust-level per-swap.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-CP-07: collectFees Q128 double truncation strands dust fees permanently
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: collectFees computes fee0 = delta0Of0/Q128 + delta0Of1/Q128, losing up to 1 wei per division (2 wei per token per call). The checkpoint advances past the remainder. Max stranded per call = 2 wei per token. Not exploitable — informational precision loss.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-CP-08: Unchecked underflow in withdrawLiquidity (value0 - redeposited0)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Precision truncation in _calculateLiquidityStartAndEndHeights REDUCES the redeposited amount (via modulo precision). The cross-side conversion uses calculateFixedSwapByRatioRoundingDown which also rounds DOWN. Both paths produce redeposited <= value. Even if underflow occurred, the wrapped value would exceed pool reserves causing token transfer revert.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-CP-09: SingleProvider partial fill fee rounding mismatch between AMM-level and pool-level
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: When amountOut > reserveOut, the fallback to swapByOutput recalculates fees independently. AMM-level adjusts proportionally. Any difference is bounded by rounding (1-2 wei). The guard at line 49 (actualAmountIn > initialAmountIn → revert) prevents user overpayment.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-CP-10: 100% fee asymmetry (input allows MAX_BPS, output rejects >= MAX_BPS)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Intentional design. Input at 100% fee: amountRemainingLessFee = 0, amountIn = 0, feeAmount = 0 → user gets 0 output, loses input to fees. Output at 100%: denominator MAX_BPS - poolFeeBPS = 0 → division by zero → must reject. Self-inflicted config error by admin (known FP pattern #4). User protected by limitAmount parameter.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-CP-03: consumedLiquidity overflow in _increaseHeight via unchecked addition
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Amount per call bounded by height's uint128 liquidity field (~3.4e38). Full uint256 wrap requires ~2^128 sequential same-direction swaps — computationally infeasible. Even if wrap occurred, checked subtractions in _collectPositionSide would revert (DoS not value extraction).
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: code-analysis: FixedHelper.sol:1864-1866 (unchecked += bounded by uint128 liquidity per call)

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-CP-05: SingleProviderPoolType TOCTOU via getPoolState VIEW calls during multi-hop swap
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: SingleProviderPoolType reads reserve state via getPoolState before each swap hop. Each hop operates on its own pool's reserves which are correct at read time. The AMM processes hops sequentially (not parallel) so each pool sees the correct pre-swap reserves for that hop.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: code-analysis: SingleProviderPoolType.sol:312-320 (reads own pool state, not cross-pool)

ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: mulDiv(uint128.max, uint128.max, Q128) = 2^128 - 2 which fits in uint128. Truncation requires delta * liquidity > Q128 * uint128.max ≈ 2^256. Fee growth wrapping (unchecked) is handled by modular arithmetic. Practical truncation unreachable.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C26: Cetus pattern — tick index overflow in computeRatioX96
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: computeRatioX96 can produce values exceeding MAX_SQRT_RATIO at extreme ratios (uint128.max:1). However, SingleProviderPoolType validates the hook's price at line 328 (< MIN_SQRT_RATIO || >= MAX_SQRT_RATIO → revert). DynamicPoolType uses tick-based pricing bounded by MIN_TICK/MAX_TICK.

Not applicable. DynamicPoolType and FixedPoolType use position-based LP (each position tracks its own liquidity). No share pool exists. SingleProviderPoolType has only one LP. The ERC-4626 share inflation attack requires share-based accounting.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C29: Hook price manipulation — mock hook returning extreme price to SingleProviderPoolType
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: SingleProviderPoolType.sol:328-329 validates hook's price against MIN_SQRT_RATIO and MAX_SQRT_RATIO bounds. Returns below min or >= max are rejected with SingleProviderPool__InvalidPrice(). Price=0 and price=type(uint160).max are both caught.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If Solidity parsed `a | b == 0` as `a | (b == 0)`, the uint256 | bool type error would prevent compilation. The code compiles, proving the compiler groups it as (a | b) == 0.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: Solidity 0.8.24 type system: uint256 | bool is not a valid expression
hypothesis_results.detail: Fuzz test over all uint256 pairs confirms `if (a | b == 0)` is equivalent to `if ((a | b) == 0)`. The operator precedence concern is a non-issue because the only type-valid parse is the intended one.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If an attacker calls addLiquidity with snapSqrtPriceX96 targeting an initialized tick in the lte direction, the `next > targetTick` check at line 264 lets it through because the tick IS the target, not between current and target.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: DynamicHelper.sol:264 — the > check is correct for lte direction by Uniswap V3 tick convention (landing on tick != crossing tick)
hypothesis_results.detail: The asymmetry between lte (>) and !lte (<=) matches Uniswap V3 semantics where the current tick is always below the current price. snapping to an initialized tick is valid because the tick's liquidityNet change is only applied on crossing.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If dust inflates the denominator in the fee split, the output-height LP receives slightly less fee and the input-height LP gets the difference. But dust is bounded by 1 input unit's output, making the skew < 3 wei per swap.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: FixedHelper.sol:1700 — dust validated against potentialDustForOneInput, bounding the denominator inflation
hypothesis_results.detail: The dust amount is bounded by calculateFixedSwapByRatio(1, packedRatio, zeroForOne) at line 1699-1700. Fee skew is proportional to dust/totalAmountOut which is negligible. Not exploitable.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If SingleProviderPoolType reads stale reserves during a multi-hop swap, the second hop could compute incorrect output. But each hop reads its OWN pool's reserves which are not modified by the first hop's pool.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: AMMModule sequential hop processing — each pool type call reads correct pre-swap state for its own pool
hypothesis_results.detail: Multi-hop swaps are processed sequentially. Each hop operates on a different pool. SingleProviderPoolType.swapByInput reads its own pool's reserves which are correct at call time.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If LPs at the last height in a swap earn more fees per unit due to accumulated truncation remainder, they could position liquidity strategically. But the remainder is bounded by numHeights-1 wei for typical amounts, not economically exploitable.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: FixedHelper.sol:1820 — final height gets all remaining feeAmount, bounded by (K-1) rounding losses
hypothesis_results.detail: Sequential mulDiv floor rounding accumulates at most 1 wei remainder per height crossed. Fuzz confirms the last height fee is bounded by totalFeeAmount. At high fee/amount ratios the absolute diff can grow but remains proportional and dust-level.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If precision truncation in _calculateLiquidityStartAndEndHeights makes redeposited0 > value0, the unchecked subtraction wraps to ~2^256 and the LP withdraws the entire pool. But precision truncation (line 360-362: add0 -= add0 % precision0) REDUCES the redeposited amount, not increases it.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: FixedHelper.sol:360-362 — precision truncation always reduces the redeposit amount
hypothesis_results.detail: Both the precision truncation and the calculateFixedSwapByRatioRoundingDown cross-side conversion round DOWN. This ensures redeposited <= value in all cases. Even if underflow occurred, the wrapped value would exceed pool token balance and the transfer would revert.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If consumedLiquidity overflows via unchecked += amount, an LP could collect inflated tokens from _collectPositionSide. But amount per call is bounded by height's uint128 liquidity (~3.4e38), requiring ~2^128 swaps to wrap a uint256.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: FixedHelper.sol:1866 — amount bounded by height liquidity (uint128), wrap requires 2^128 calls
hypothesis_results.detail: Computationally infeasible to overflow. Even if wrap occurred, checked subtractions in _collectPositionSide (lines 508, 513) would revert on underflow, creating DoS rather than value extraction.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If pool-type and AMM-level fee calculations use different rounding, the total fees may not sum correctly, creating a token accounting error. But both use mulDivRoundingUp for fee calculation and the guard at line 49 prevents user overpayment.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: SingleProviderHelper.sol:49 — swapCache.amountIn > initialAmountIn reverts, preventing overpayment
hypothesis_results.detail: Any rounding difference between AMM-level proportional adjustment and pool-level independent calculation is bounded by 1-2 wei. The amountIn guard prevents the user from paying more than their initial input.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If Q128 double truncation strands fees, an attacker could repeatedly collect to drain more than their share while others' fees are stranded. But the truncation only LOSES up to 2 wei per token per call — it never CREATES extra tokens.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: FixedHelper.sol:577-580 — each division loses at most 1 wei, fee checkpoint advance at 582-585 is atomic
hypothesis_results.detail: Max stranded per collectFees call = 2 wei per token (from 4 independent floor divisions). The checkpoint advances atomically so the remainder is permanently lost, not reclaimable. This is informational dust-level precision loss, not a finding.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If a pool hook returns 10000 BPS (100% fee) for input swaps, the swapper loses their entire input with 0 output. But this requires an admin to deliberately set the fee to 100%, which is a self-inflicted config error (known FP pattern #4 in audit_memory).
hypothesis_results.guard_location: User protection via limitAmount parameter in swap — user can set minimum output. Also: admin-set fee is self-inflicted config error.
hypothesis_results.detail: The asymmetry is intentional: input swaps can have 100% fee (result: 0 swap, all goes to fee), output swaps cannot (would require division by zero). Both paths are consistent. The user's limitAmount parameter protects against receiving 0 output.
